claim: QSS supports all CSS2 selectors plus Qt sub-controls (::handle, ::item, ::indicator, ::drop-down, ::add-line...) and a large pseudo-state set including :hover, :pressed, :disabled, :checked, :indeterminate, :focus, :selected, :read-only, :default, :flat, :on/:off, :open/:closed, :active — states are chainable and negatable (:!hover).
verbatim_quote: Qt Style Sheets support all the selectors defined in CSS2... Pseudo-states can be negated using the exclamation operator... Pseudo-states can be chained, in which case a logical AND is implied.
quote: Qt Style Sheets support all the selectors defined in CSS2... Pseudo-states can be negated using the exclamation operator... Pseudo-states can be chained, in which case a logical AND is implied.

claim: border-radius works on nearly every widget a control panel needs (buttons, line edits, frames/cards, labels, menus, checkboxes, combo boxes, item views, tooltips) with per-corner variants; it clips the element's background.
verbatim_quote: The border-radius clips the element's background. This property is supported by QAbstractItemView subclasses, QAbstractSpinBox subclasses, QCheckBox, QComboBox, QFrame, QGroupBox, QLabel, QLineEdit, QMenu, QMenuBar, QPushButton, QRadioButton, QSplitter, QTextEdit, and QToolTip.
quote: The border-radius clips the element's background. This property is supported by QAbstractItemView subclasses, QAbstractSpinBox subclasses, QCheckBox, QComboBox, QFrame, QGroupBox, QLabel, QLineEdit, QMenu, QMenuBar, QPushButton, QRadioButton, QSplitter, QTextEdit, and QToolTip.

claim: QSS has no transition/transform/box-shadow/filter/animation properties — the supported property list is a closed set of box-model, color, font, border, image and Qt-specific extras; CSS-style state transitions are impossible in QSS itself.
verbatim_quote: This section lists all the properties supported by Qt Style Sheets. Which values can be given to a property depend on the property's type.
quote: This section lists all the properties supported by Qt Style Sheets. Which values can be given to a property depend on the property's type.

claim: The QSS opacity property exists but applies only to tooltips — per-widget translucency is NOT available via QSS; use QGraphicsOpacityEffect or windowOpacity (top-level only).
verbatim_quote: The opacity for a widget. Possible values are from 0 (transparent) to 255 (opaque). For the moment, this is only supported for tooltips.
quote: The opacity for a widget. Possible values are from 0 (transparent) to 255 (opaque). For the moment, this is only supported for tooltips.

claim: widget-animation-duration in QSS only scales the style's own hint animations (SH_Widget_Animation_Duration); it does not create CSS-style transitions between pseudo-states.
verbatim_quote: How much an animation should last (in milliseconds). A value equal to zero means that the animations will be disabled. If this property is not specified, it defaults to the value specified by the current style for the SH_Widget_Animation_Duration style hint.
quote: How much an animation should last (in milliseconds). A value equal to zero means that the animations will be disabled. If this property is not specified, it defaults to the value specified by the current style for the SH_Widget_Animation_Duration style hint.

claim: QLabel does not support the :hover pseudo-state — pill/badge labels needing hover must be custom-painted or replaced by QToolButton/QPushButton.
verbatim_quote: Supports the box model. Does not support the :hover pseudo-state.
quote: Supports the box model. Does not support the :hover pseudo-state.

claim: A custom QWidget subclass only supports background/background-clip/background-origin in QSS and will not render the stylesheet at all without a paintEvent that calls style()->drawPrimitive(PE_Widget).
verbatim_quote: Supports only the background, background-clip and background-origin properties. If you subclass from QWidget, you need to provide a paintEvent for your custom QWidget... style()->drawPrimitive(QStyle::PE_Widget, &opt, &p, this);
quote: Supports only the background, background-clip and background-origin properties. If you subclass from QWidget, you need to provide a paintEvent for your custom QWidget... style()->drawPrimitive(QStyle::PE_Widget, &opt, &p, this);

claim: QSS has no !important and no font/color inheritance — children do not inherit font/color from a styled parent; selectors like 'QGroupBox, QGroupBox *' are needed.
verbatim_quote: Be aware that Qt currently doesn't implement !important... By default, when using Qt Style Sheets, a widget does not automatically inherit its font and color setting from its parent widget.
quote: Be aware that Qt currently doesn't implement !important... By default, when using Qt Style Sheets, a widget does not automatically inherit its font and color setting from its parent widget.

claim: qproperty-* values in QSS are evaluated once at polish time, so they cannot react to pseudo-states — they cannot be used to animate or toggle widget properties on hover.
verbatim_quote: the qproperty syntax is evaluated only once, which is when the widget is polished by the style. This means that any attempt to use them in pseudo-states such as QPushButton:hover, will not work.
quote: the qproperty syntax is evaluated only once, which is when the widget is polished by the style. This means that any attempt to use them in pseudo-states such as QPushButton:hover, will not work.

claim: Qt officially positions style sheets as a prototyping/small-adjustment tool, not the production styling mechanism; production UIs should use a QStyle subclass (or the new Qt Labs StyleKit, QStyleKitStyle, since Qt 6.12 — API may change).
verbatim_quote: They are a tool for prototyping and for small, local adjustments, not for the production look of an application... QStyleKitStyle is available since Qt 6.12. StyleKit is a Qt Labs module, and its API may change between Qt releases.
quote: They are a tool for prototyping and for small, local adjustments, not for the production look of an application... QStyleKitStyle is available since Qt 6.12. StyleKit is a Qt Labs module, and its API may change between Qt releases.

claim: QSS perf model: every affected widget is drawn through a wrapping 'style sheet' engine that matches selectors and caches render rules per widget — cost grows with widget count × rule count; complex selector trees on hundreds of widgets is the slow path.
verbatim_quote: Every affected widget is drawn through the style sheet engine... For each widget it matches the selectors against the widget's class, object name, properties, and state, computes the rendering rules, and caches them per widget. The memory and processing cost grows with the number of widgets and rules.
quote: Every affected widget is drawn through the style sheet engine... For each widget it matches the selectors against the widget's class, object name, properties, and state, computes the rendering rules, and caches them per widget. The memory and processing cost grows with the number of widgets and rules.

claim: Calling setStyleSheet (app- or widget-level) repolishes everything it applies to — recomputing fonts, palettes, geometry, size hints, with possible flicker; runtime theme switching via QSS is officially discouraged.
verbatim_quote: Each call to QApplication::setStyleSheet() discards the caches and repolishes every widget in the application, which recomputes fonts, palettes, geometry, and size hints and can visibly flicker. Don't build theme switching on style sheets.
quote: Each call to QApplication::setStyleSheet() discards the caches and repolishes every widget in the application, which recomputes fonts, palettes, geometry, and size hints and can visibly flicker. Don't build theme switching on style sheets.

claim: Per-widget setStyleSheet with formatted strings is a perf trap: the sheet is re-parsed per widget and repolishes the widget + all children even when the string is unchanged; the recommended pattern is one app-level sheet + dynamic-property selectors.
verbatim_quote: A style sheet set on a widget is parsed once for every widget it's set on, not once for every string, and each call to QWidget::setStyleSheet() repolishes the widget and all its children, even when the string didn't change... Instead, express the difference with a selector on an object name or a Qt property in the one style sheet.
quote: A style sheet set on a widget is parsed once for every widget it's set on, not once for every string, and each call to QWidget::setStyleSheet() repolishes the widget and all its children, even when the string didn't change... Instead, express the difference with a selector on an object name or a Qt property in the one style sheet.

claim: A partial QSS rule discards the native look for the whole element — e.g. setting only a QPushButton background yields a flat borderless button, so you must then specify borders, padding and every state yourself (the 'all-or-nothing' effect).
verbatim_quote: When a rule requests something the native style cannot honor, such as a background color for a QPushButton, the style sheet engine draws the whole element itself, without the native decoration. You then have to specify borders, padding, and every state yourself, and a small adjustment grows into a complete description of the look.
quote: When a rule requests something the native style cannot honor, such as a background color for a QPushButton, the style sheet engine draws the whole element itself, without the native decoration. You then have to specify borders, padding, and every state yourself, and a small adjustment grows into a complete description of the look.

claim: QSS wins over setFont/setPalette/item colors — programmatic color changes become silent no-ops once a stylesheet covers that role.
verbatim_quote: A style sheet overrides fonts, palettes, and item colors set with functions such as QWidget::setFont() or QTreeWidgetItem::setBackground(), so the styling of a widget is no longer visible in one place.
quote: A style sheet overrides fonts, palettes, and item colors set with functions such as QWidget::setFont() or QTreeWidgetItem::setBackground(), so the styling of a widget is no longer visible in one place.

claim: palette(role) color values (e.g. 'color: palette(window)') let a stylesheet follow the application palette incl. dark scheme — preferred over hard-coded hex for theme-safe QSS.
verbatim_quote: Use palette(window), palette(text), and the other palette roles so that the style sheet follows the application palette, including a dark color scheme.
quote: Use palette(window), palette(text), and the other palette roles so that the style sheet follows the application palette, including a dark color scheme.

claim: em/ex lengths are supported in QSS and recommended over px for font-following paddings/margins; pt for font sizes — px scales with display DPI but not user font size.
verbatim_quote: Use em and ex lengths for paddings, margins, and sizes that should follow the font, and pt for font sizes.
quote: Use em and ex lengths for paddings, margins, and sizes that should follow the font, and pt for font sizes.

claim: Scrollbar styling is fully achievable in QSS (::handle, ::add-line, ::sub-line, ::add-page, ::sub-page, arrows, width/height, margins, subcontrol-position/origin, position:absolute) but is all-or-nothing: customize one part and you must style every other sub-control.
verbatim_quote: The QScrollBar can be styled using its subcontrols like handle, add-line, sub-line, and so on. Note that if one property or sub-control is customized, all the other properties or sub-controls must be customized as well.
quote: The QScrollBar can be styled using its subcontrols like handle, add-line, sub-line, and so on. Note that if one property or sub-control is customized, all the other properties or sub-controls must be customized as well.

claim: QMenu is fully styleable: ::item padding/border, :selected state (incl. rgba alpha), ::separator, ::indicator, ::icon:checked, ::right-arrow for submenus; reserving a transparent border on items avoids layout shift on selection.
verbatim_quote: QMenu::item { padding: 2px 25px 2px 20px; border: 1px solid transparent; /* reserve space for selection border */ } QMenu::item:selected { border-color: darkblue; background: rgba(100, 100, 100, 150); }
quote: QMenu::item { padding: 2px 25px 2px 20px; border: 1px solid transparent; /* reserve space for selection border */ } QMenu::item:selected { border-color: darkblue; background: rgba(100, 100, 100, 150); }

claim: QSS box model is real margin/border/padding/content; render order is: clip by border-radius → background-image → border/border-image → overlay image. background-image does NOT scale with the widget — use 9-slice border-image for scalable surfaces, or the image property which accepts SVG and auto-scales.
verbatim_quote: A background-image does not scale with the size of the widget. To provide a 'skin' or background that scales along with the widget size, one must use border-image... Unlike background-image and border-image, one may specify a SVG in the image property, in which case the image is scaled automatically according to the widget size.
quote: A background-image does not scale with the size of the widget. To provide a 'skin' or background that scales along with the widget size, one must use border-image... Unlike background-image and border-image, one may specify a SVG in the image property, in which case the image is scaled automatically according to the widget size.

claim: Dynamic-property selectors ('*[mandatoryField="true"] {...}') are the official pattern for state-driven styling — setProperty() then repolish; but selectors are NOT re-evaluated automatically when the property changes (KDAB: 'forcing hacks such as reset of a style sheet' — in PyQt: widget.style().unpolish(w); widget.style().polish(w)).
verbatim_quote: There are many situations where we need to present a form that has mandatory fields... *[mandatoryField="true"] { background-color: yellow }
quote: There are many situations where we need to present a form that has mandatory fields... *[mandatoryField="true"] { background-color: yellow }

claim: KDAB's verdict on QSS ceilings: no solution exists for unsupported customizations ('If there's no support for a specific customization, there's no solution'), QSS does not mix with QProxyStyle/custom QStyle, has no include mechanism, and reparenting a widget clears the stylesheet rule cache (perf hit in dynamic UIs).
verbatim_quote: Style sheets allow you to do a number of things, but not everything. If there's no support for a specific customization, there's no solution... Each reparenting triggers clearing the stylesheet rules cache and recalculating everything... no include mechanism
quote: Style sheets allow you to do a number of things, but not everything. If there's no support for a specific customization, there's no solution... Each reparenting triggers clearing the stylesheet rules cache and recalculating everything... no include mechanism

claim: QVariantAnimation interpolates QColor natively — this is the standard mechanism for smooth hover/pressed color transitions that QSS cannot express; connect valueChanged to a slot storing the color + update(), then consume it in paintEvent or via a pyqtProperty.
verbatim_quote: Not all QVariant types are supported. Below is a list of currently supported QVariant types: [includes] QColor... QVariantAnimation will interpolate the property of the target object and emit valueChanged().
quote: Not all QVariant types are supported. Below is a list of currently supported QVariant types: [includes] QColor... QVariantAnimation will interpolate the property of the target object and emit valueChanged().

claim: QPropertyAnimation animates any Qt property with a setter — official example animates a widget's 'pos'; applies to geometry, pos, size, windowOpacity, and custom pyqtProperty(QColor/...) declarations; default duration 250ms, easing via QEasingCurve, grouping via QParallelAnimationGroup.
verbatim_quote: Note that this makes it possible to animate many of Qt's widgets... QPropertyAnimation *anim = new QPropertyAnimation(button, "pos", this); ... The default duration is 250ms.
quote: Note that this makes it possible to animate many of Qt's widgets... QPropertyAnimation *anim = new QPropertyAnimation(button, "pos", this); ... The default duration is 250ms.

claim: QGraphicsDropShadowEffect is the box-shadow workaround — color, offset (QPointF), blurRadius properties; defaults: QColor(63,63,63,180), radius 1, offset 8px lower-right. blurRadius/offset are Qt properties so shadows can be animated on hover.
verbatim_quote: By default, the drop shadow is a semi-transparent dark gray (QColor(63, 63, 63, 180)) shadow, blurred with a radius of 1 at an offset of 8 pixels towards the lower right.
quote: By default, the drop shadow is a semi-transparent dark gray (QColor(63, 63, 63, 180)) shadow, blurred with a radius of 1 at an offset of 8 pixels towards the lower right.

claim: Hard limits of graphics effects: only ONE effect per widget (installing a new one deletes the old), it applies to the widget AND ALL ITS CHILDREN (whole subtree re-rendered via offscreen pixmap every repaint), and it does not work on OpenGL widgets.
verbatim_quote: If there already is an effect installed on this widget, QWidget will delete the existing effect before installing the new effect... This function will apply the effect on itself and all its children... Graphics effects are not supported for OpenGL-based widgets
quote: If there already is an effect installed on this widget, QWidget will delete the existing effect before installing the new effect... This function will apply the effect on itself and all its children... Graphics effects are not supported for OpenGL-based widgets

claim: Graphics effects render the source to an offscreen pixmap that is then composited (sourcePixmap mechanism) — a DropShadow on a busy card re-renders the whole subtree each repaint; keep effects on small, mostly-static leaf containers rather than frequently-updating widgets.
verbatim_quote: In the draw() function you can call sourcePixmap() to get a pixmap of the graphics effect source which you can then process.
quote: In the draw() function you can call sourcePixmap() to get a pixmap of the graphics effect source which you can then process.

claim: QScrollArea mechanics: widgetResizable=True auto-resizes the content widget to avoid scrollbars where avoidable; scroll bar visibility follows Qt::ScrollBarPolicy — and when a scrollbar appears/disappears the viewport shrinks/expands, causing layout shift (fix: ScrollBarAlwaysOn or an overlaid custom scrollbar; Qt Widgets has no built-in overlay/auto-fade scrollbar — AsNeeded just toggles visibility).
verbatim_quote: When a scroll bar is hidden, the viewport expands in order to cover all available space. When a scroll bar becomes visible again, the viewport shrinks in order to make room for the scroll bar.
quote: When a scroll bar is hidden, the viewport expands in order to cover all available space. When a scroll bar becomes visible again, the viewport shrinks in order to make room for the scroll bar.

claim: Overlay/floating scrollbars do not exist in Qt Widgets out of the box — QAbstractScrollArea only offers policy-driven real scroll bar widgets placed beside the viewport; an overlay scrollbar would need a custom widget painted on top of the viewport (macOS does it natively via the platform style).
verbatim_quote: Next to the viewport is a vertical scroll bar, and below is a horizontal scroll bar. When all of the area contents fits in the viewport, each scroll bar can be either visible or hidden depending on the scroll bar's Qt::ScrollBarPolicy.
quote: Next to the viewport is a vertical scroll bar, and below is a horizontal scroll bar. When all of the area contents fits in the viewport, each scroll bar can be either visible or hidden depending on the scroll bar's Qt::ScrollBarPolicy.

claim: QFont::setFeature(tag, value) exists since Qt 6.7 — full OpenType feature access from PyQt6, e.g. font.setFeature(QFont.Tag.fromString('tnum'), 1) enables tabular figures in fonts that ship them; setFeature overrides Qt's defaults (kern tied to kerning(), ligatures disabled when letterSpacing applied).
verbatim_quote: [since 6.7] void QFont::setFeature(QFont::Tag tag, quint32 value) — Applies an integer value to the typographical feature specified by tag when shaping the text. This provides advanced access to the font shaping process, and can be used to support font features that are otherwise not covered in the API.
quote: [since 6.7] void QFont::setFeature(QFont::Tag tag, quint32 value) — Applies an integer value to the typographical feature specified by tag when shaping the text. This provides advanced access to the font shaping process, and can be used to support font features that are otherwise not covered in the API.

claim: Segoe UI is Windows' built-in UI font (default since Vista) with native Cyrillic coverage (code page 1251, plus Latin/Greek/Arabic/Hebrew etc.) — safe zero-dependency choice for a Russian dark UI; Segoe UI Variable is the Win11 variant of the same family.
verbatim_quote: It became Microsoft's default user interface font with the release of Windows Vista in 2007... Segoe UI supports a very wide range of languages and scripts, including the Latin, Greek, and Cyrillic alphabets... Code pages: ... 1251 Cyrillic ...
quote: It became Microsoft's default user interface font with the release of Windows Vista in 2007... Segoe UI supports a very wide range of languages and scripts, including the Latin, Greek, and Cyrillic alphabets... Code pages: ... 1251 Cyrillic ...

claim: Consolas is the Windows-bundled monospace with full Cyrillic (code pages 1251, 866 MS-DOS Russian, 855 IBM Cyrillic) and OpenType features incl. lining/hanging numerals — usable for metrics/log columns with zero install.
verbatim_quote: Consolas is aimed for use in programming environments and other circumstances where a monospaced font is specified... OpenType features include hanging or lining numerals... Code pages: ... 1251 Cyrillic ... 866 MS-DOS Russian ...
quote: Consolas is aimed for use in programming environments and other circumstances where a monospaced font is specified... OpenType features include hanging or lining numerals... Code pages: ... 1251 Cyrillic ... 866 MS-DOS Russian ...

claim: Inter (if installed or shipped — OFL, embeddable via QFontDatabase.addApplicationFont) has 2000+ glyphs, 147 languages incl. full Cyrillic block, weights 100–900, variable wght+opsz axes, and a dedicated tnum feature with equal-width figures across all weights — the best tabular-numbers option for dashboards.
verbatim_quote: tnum Tabular numbers — Fixed-width numbers are useful for tabular data, where comparing columns across rows is desired... `tnum` enables an entire set of dedicated glyphs that have the same width across all weights.
quote: tnum Tabular numbers — Fixed-width numbers are useful for tabular data, where comparing columns across rows is desired... `tnum` enables an entire set of dedicated glyphs that have the same width across all weights.

claim: Dark native title bar on Windows is one ctypes call: DwmSetWindowAttribute(hwnd, DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE, TRUE) makes the window frame render in dark-mode colors — windows default to light frame regardless of system setting, so a dark app needs this explicitly.
verbatim_quote: DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE — Use with DwmSetWindowAttribute. Allows the window frame for this window to be drawn in dark mode colors when the dark mode system setting is enabled. For compatibility reasons, all windows default to light mode regardless of the system setting.
quote: DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE — Use with DwmSetWindowAttribute. Allows the window frame for this window to be drawn in dark mode colors when the dark mode system setting is enabled. For compatibility reasons, all windows default to light mode regardless of the system setting.

claim: Mica/Acrylic on Windows 11 (build 22621+) is achievable via DwmSetWindowAttribute(hwnd, DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE, DWMSBT_*): DWMSBT_MAINWINDOW=Mica, DWMSBT_TRANSIENTWINDOW=Desktop Acrylic, DWMSBT_TABBEDWINDOW=Mica Alt — plain dwmapi call, reachable from PyQt6 via ctypes on int(winId()).
verbatim_quote: DWMSBT_MAINWINDOW — Draw the backdrop material effect corresponding to a long-lived window behind the entire window bounds. For Windows 11, this corresponds to Mica in its default variant... Minimum supported client: Windows 11 Build 22621
quote: DWMSBT_MAINWINDOW — Draw the backdrop material effect corresponding to a long-lived window behind the entire window bounds. For Windows 11, this corresponds to Mica in its default variant... Minimum supported client: Windows 11 Build 22621

claim: Rounded window corners can also be controlled via DwmSetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_WINDOW_CORNER_PREFERENCE) — relevant for frameless windows on Win11.
verbatim_quote: DWMWA_WINDOW_CORNER_PREFERENCE — Use with DwmSetWindowAttribute. Specifies the rounded corner preference for a window.
quote: DWMWA_WINDOW_CORNER_PREFERENCE — Use with DwmSetWindowAttribute. Specifies the rounded corner preference for a window.

claim: A full modern frameless window IS achievable in PyQt6/PySide6 on Windows — PyQt-Frameless-Window (zhiyiYo) implements moving, resizing/stretching, native window shadow, snap layouts, Win10 acrylic, Win11 mica, Win7 aero via pywin32/ctypes; known caveats: moving an acrylic window on Win10 can get stuck, snap layout not enabled by default.
verbatim_quote: Moving / Stretching / Window shadow / Window animation / Win11 snap layout / Win10 acrylic blur / Win11 mica blur / Win7 Aero blur... Moving the acrylic window on Win10 may get stuck. At present, there is no good solution.
quote: Moving / Stretching / Window shadow / Window animation / Win11 snap layout / Win10 acrylic blur / Win11 mica blur / Win7 Aero blur... Moving the acrylic window on Win10 may get stuck. At present, there is no good solution.

claim: The polished-PyQt reference implementation (QFluentWidgets) uses a hybrid: per-widget QSS for base theming (FluentStyleSheet.BUTTON.apply) + manual isHover/isPressed flags via enter/leave/mouse events + custom paintEvent with antialiased QPainter + pyqtProperty(QColor) animatable color properties + dedicated animation helpers — i.e. modern state-layer visuals are painted, not stylesheeted.
verbatim_quote:
def enterEvent(self, e):
    self.isHover = True
    self.update()
... lightTextColor = pyqtProperty(QColor, getLightTextColor, setLightTextColor)
... painter.setRenderHints(QPainter.Antialiasing | QPainter.SmoothPixmapTransform)
quote:
def enterEvent(self, e):
    self.isHover = True
    self.update()
... lightTextColor = pyqtProperty(QColor, getLightTextColor, setLightTextColor)
... painter.setRenderHints(QPainter.Antialiasing | QPainter.SmoothPixmapTransform)

claim: PyQtDarkTheme shows the mature approach for app-wide theming: dark QPalette + a single application-level QSS (forked from QDarkStyleSheet) + OS theme sync — it does not attempt per-widget custom painting, which is why its look is 'flat modern' rather than Fluent-level polished.
verbatim_quote: PyQtDarkTheme applies a flat dark theme to QtWidgets application... qdarktheme.load_palette(theme="dark"), qdarktheme.load_stylesheet(theme="dark")... Qt stylesheets are originally fork of QDarkStyleSheet.
quote: PyQtDarkTheme applies a flat dark theme to QtWidgets application... qdarktheme.load_palette(theme="dark"), qdarktheme.load_stylesheet(theme="dark")... Qt stylesheets are originally fork of QDarkStyleSheet.

claim: Qt 6 on Windows is Per-Monitor DPI Aware V2 by default — no manifest work needed in PyQt6; fractional scale factors (125%/150%) can produce artifacts, mitigated by QGuiApplication.setHighDpiScaleFactorRoundingPolicy (env QT_SCALE_FACTOR_ROUNDING_POLICY=Round, default PassThrough).
verbatim_quote: Qt 6 is Per-Monitor DPI Aware V2 by default... Integer scale factors (for example, 1.0 or 2.0) are preferred for best results... it can use QGuiApplication::setHighDpiScaleFactorRoundingPolicy() to limit the scale factors it sees.
quote: Qt 6 is Per-Monitor DPI Aware V2 by default... Integer scale factors (for example, 1.0 or 2.0) are preferred for best results... it can use QGuiApplication::setHighDpiScaleFactorRoundingPolicy() to limit the scale factors it sees.

claim: Set the application stylesheet once on QApplication before the first window shows — changing it at runtime 'can lead to inconsistent results where only some parts of the previous style sheet are reverted'; when a stylesheet is active, QWidget::style() returns a wrapper 'style sheet' style (windows11 style underneath on Windows in Qt 6.12+).
verbatim_quote: Set the application style sheet once, before the first window is shown. Changing the style sheet at runtime can lead to inconsistent results where only some parts of the previous style sheet are reverted by the new style sheet. Don't use this function to switch themes at runtime.
quote: Set the application style sheet once, before the first window is shown. Changing the style sheet at runtime can lead to inconsistent results where only some parts of the previous style sheet are reverted by the new style sheet. Don't use this function to switch themes at runtime.

claim: QSS url() values can reference arbitrary local files/Qt resources — a stylesheet built from untrusted input can make the app read and display local files; keep .qss bundled in resources or hardcoded.
verbatim_quote: the url() function can point at any local file or Qt resource... A malicious style sheet can cause Qt to read and display the contents of arbitrary local files that the application process has permission to access.
quote: the url() function can point at any local file or Qt resource... A malicious style sheet can cause Qt to read and display the contents of arbitrary local files that the application process has permission to access.

claim: HiDPI 'just works' for Qt6 bindings (PyQtDarkTheme's enable_hi_dpi() is only needed for Qt5) — confirms no special DPI setup is required in PyQt6 apps.
verbatim_quote: For Qt6 bindings, HiDPI 'just works' without using this function.
quote: For Qt6 bindings, HiDPI 'just works' without using this function.

claim: For frameless windows the naive Qt::FramelessWindowHint approach loses native behaviors (resize borders, snap layout, DWM shadow); the win32 message/DWM route (WM_NCHITTEST handling + DwmSetWindowAttribute) is what preserves them — evidenced by PyQt-Frameless-Window implementing snapping/shadow via pywin32 rather than Qt APIs.
verbatim_quote: Features: Moving / Stretching / Window shadow / Window animation / Win11 snap layout... | Win32 | pywin32 |
quote: Features: Moving / Stretching / Window shadow / Window animation / Win11 snap layout... | Win32 | pywin32 |

claim: The 'proper' Microsoft-documented path for Mica in Win32 is MicaController via Windows App SDK + WinRT Compositor + DispatcherQueue — heavyweight; the lightweight DwmSetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE) route used by PyQt-Frameless-Window achieves the same visual result without the SDK.
verbatim_quote: To apply Mica to a Win32 app for Windows 11, you need to use the Windows App SDK... you use the MicaController class. This class manages both the rendering of the system backdrop material as well as the handling of system policy for the mica material.
quote: To apply Mica to a Win32 app for Windows 11, you need to use the Windows App SDK... you use the MicaController class. This class manages both the rendering of the system backdrop material as well as the handling of system policy for the mica material.
